Liverpool defender Andy Robertson has emphasized that strengthening the team's defensive performance will be crucial for new manager Arne Slot to mount a serious championship bid during his inaugural campaign at the helm. The Scottish left-back highlighted the importance of maintaining defensive solidity as the Reds prepare for their challenging upcoming fixture against Manchester United at Old Trafford, where their defensive unit is expected to face a significantly tougher examination than in their previous outings. While Liverpool has managed to keep clean sheets in both of their initial matches under Slot's guidance, Robertson acknowledges that the true test of their defensive capabilities lies ahead, particularly in high-stakes encounters against traditional rivals and top-tier opposition.

Handle the defensive statistics from the previous campaign reveals a concerning pattern that Robertson believes must be addressed if Liverpool hopes to compete effectively for the Premier League crown. During the 2023-24 season, the Merseyside club allowed 41 goals across their 38 league fixtures while securing a third-place finish, a defensive record that compared unfavorably to their title-contending rivals. The eventual champions Manchester City demonstrated superior defensive discipline by conceding just 34 goals throughout the campaign, while Arsenal, who finished as runners-up, showcased even more impressive defensive statistics by allowing only 29 goals against them. Robertson's analysis suggests that this defensive vulnerability ultimately cost Liverpool in their pursuit of silverware, as he noted that even during periods when they remained in contention for the title, they were consistently allowing more scoring opportunities to their opponents compared to the teams that finished above them.

The Scotland international expressed optimism about the early defensive displays under Slot's tactical system, with victories against Ipswich Town and Brentford both resulting in clean sheets and providing an ideal platform for the new era at Anfield. Robertson's comments reflect a clear understanding that sustainable success requires a more disciplined defensive approach, particularly in matches where opponents create multiple chances and the margin for error becomes minimal. Looking ahead to the Manchester United clash and the fixtures following the international break, Robertson stressed the importance of limiting opposition opportunities and maintaining the defensive standards established in the opening matches. His acknowledgment that Liverpool's tendency to concede numerous chances eventually led to their downfall in crucial matches last season demonstrates a mature assessment of the team's shortcomings and a determination to rectify these issues under their new Dutch manager's philosophy.

P.S. Robertson's honest evaluation of Liverpool's defensive frailties from last season and his emphasis on improvement under Slot suggests a renewed focus on building championship-winning foundations from the back.
